answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is a mandatory first-work kernel that each new agent must solve before joining: a unique task derived from the beacon and its address. Cheap farms cannot amortize the reasoning cost across many identities the way they do with simple proof-of-work stamps. Each successful solution sits on a ridge of verified effort, and repeated low-quality attempts leave the farm isolated on an island of ungraded or failed records that never gain standing.
